subject: Clarify execution locality, subprocessor roles, and cross-border transfer paths
messages:
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@orchid.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-23T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial Qs on where request data is executed and subprocessors (Orchid Security Questionnaire attached)

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks for taking the time to chat last week. The security team here at Orchid asked me to formalize a few follow-ups so we can evaluate Redwood for our inference stack. Attached is our security questionnaire — the three items we need clarified up front are:

1) Where are inference requests executed (region / cloud / GPU host)? If a user in the EU interacts with our app, can you guarantee processing inside EU regions?

2) Which subprocessors have access to request payloads or KV/prefix caches, and where are those subprocessors located? We need names + regions and whether they can decrypt or access raw content.

3) Cross-border transfer mechanics: if processing is routed for performance or fallback, how are transfers logged and controlled? Any contractual or SCCs you rely on?

We attached the questionnaire and highlighted the above. Can you respond in writing and include any evidence (region map, subprocessor inventory, SOC2 / DPA references)?

Best,
Sara Jensen
Head of Security, Orchid Health

Attachment: Orchid_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@orchid.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-23T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial Qs on where request data is executed and subprocessors (Orchid Security Questionnaire attached)

Hi Sara — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. Quick note to confirm we received the questionnaire.

We can definitely provide a written summary and evidence pack. High-level answers up front while we assemble attachments:
- Execution locality: requests are executed in the region you select (we expose region pinning for hosted workloads). We operate in eu-west-1, eu-central-1, us-east-1, and ap-southeast-1 for hosted customers.
- Subprocessors: core infra providers (AWS, GCP, Azure depending on region) and a small set of managed services for observability & monitoring. No external party can decrypt customer prompt data at rest without a customer key when using our Private deployment.
- Cross-border: routing policies are configurable; we default to region-first, then failover within the same jurisdiction where possible. We use SCCs + DPA; we will include language and evidence.

I attached a short region map and our subprocessor inventory CSV for your security team to review; Marissa will follow up with the detailed Q&A and the SOC2/DPA links. If helpful we can do a 30-minute walkthrough this week to go through the attachments line-by-line.

Would Thu 07/26 10:00am CET / 1:00am PDT work for a short call? (If not, propose times.)

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-regions-summary.pdf, redwood-subprocessor-inventory.csv

From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@orchid.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-24T16:20:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Initial Qs on where request data is executed and subprocessors (Orchid Security Questionnaire attached)

Thanks Jordan — that covers a lot. A few follow-ups from our side before we schedule a call:

- Residency guarantee: when you say "region pinning for hosted workloads", can you share the SLA-like guarantee text? We need to know what exceptions exist (e.g., failover, maintenance, autoscale bursts).

- KV/prefix cache: can you confirm if cached KV/prefix information is stored within the same region as execution and for how long? Is that subject to the same deletion workflow?

- Subprocessor detail: we need exact subprocessor names and the roles that allow access to request payloads or caches (read-only telemetry vs. admin tooling vs. access to persistent storage). A CSV is helpful but we also need a brief description per vendor.

- Legal: do you rely on SCCs only, or also on additional derogations / BCRs? We may require a signed DPA with specific transfer clauses.

If you can send the draft DPA / SCC references and a short matrix that maps: component -> subprocessor -> access scope -> region, that would let us triage quickly.

Best,
Sara

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@orchid.health>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-25T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial Qs on where request data is executed and subprocessors (Orchid Security Questionnaire attached)

Hi Sara — appreciate the detail. Below is a concise matrix-style reply that addresses each of your bullets; I’ll also attach a one-page evidence summary and links to our legal artifacts.

1) Region pinning & exceptions
- What we offer: Hosted customers can select a primary execution region per API key or per workspace. We commit to region-local execution for production traffic unless the customer enables cross-region fallback.
- Exceptions: emergency failover (explicitly enabled via configuration), capacity overflow (autoscale burst may temporarily use other regions in the same jurisdiction), and scheduled maintenance where we notify customers 48 hours in advance where possible.
- Example policy text: "Redwood will route inference requests to the customer-selected primary region. Cross-region routing will not occur unless (a) the customer has enabled cross-region failover, (b) there is a region-wide outage and no compatible capacity exists, or (c) a mutually agreed emergency response is required." We can include this clause in the DPA or addendum.

2) Cache and KV locality + deletion workflows
- KV/prefix caches are created and stored in the execution region by default. Ephemeral caches (per-request KV) are retained in-memory and persisted to region-local encrypted storage for up to 48 hours for reuse and autoscaling efficiency, unless you configure a shorter TTL.
- Deletion: API-level deletion requests trigger removal from hot caches immediately; persistent storage deletion follows our data lifecycle with a 30-day soft-delete window and a 90-day physical purge timeline for hosted customers. Private deployments can opt for shorter purge windows. We include audit records for deletion requests in our logs.

3) Subprocessor inventory & roles (summary)
- Cloud compute & storage: AWS (eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west1), Azure (westeurope) — role: managed compute/storage; cannot decrypt customer payloads when you use customer-managed keys in Private deployments.
- Monitoring & metrics: Datadog (EU region instances where possible) — role: observability (aggregated telemetry only; no access to raw prompts).
- Logging & alerting: SumoLogic / internal ELK (region-local) — role: retention of logs and audit trails; raw request snippets are redacted in telemetry unless explicitly allowed for debugging with a signed request.
- Support & runbook access: our on-call engineers (Redwood staff) have access via authenticated tooling; access to customer data is logged and gated by role-based approvals.

We will provide a CSV + one-line description per vendor in the evidence pack (attached). For each vendor we include the primary operating region and data access scope.

4) Legal controls and transfers
- Baseline: DPA + SCCs (European Commission standard contractual clauses).
- Additional controls: where customers require it, we offer: (a) explicit contractual addenda restricting cross-region failover, (b) Private deployment with customer-managed keys (no Redwood staff decrypting data), and (c) enterprise-only clauses around logging retention and audit support.

Evidence we attached / links provided:
- redwood-regions-summary.pdf (map of active regions & availability zones)
- redwood-subprocessor-inventory.csv (vendor, role, primary region, access scope)
- SOC2 report link: https://drive.redwood.ai/reports/SOC2-2028
- Draft DPA + SCC references: https://legal.redwood.ai/DPA-draft-2028.pdf

Next steps:
- If you want a walkthrough, Jordan can run through the CSV and region map.
- If Orchid needs a customized addendum (narrower failover, shorter purge), please flag which clauses to modify and we’ll route to legal.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Product — Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-inventory.csv, redwood-regions-summary.pdf

From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@orchid.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-25T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial Qs on where request data is executed and subprocessors (Orchid Security Questionnaire attached)

Marissa — this is exactly the level of detail we needed, thank you. Two quick asks before we move to legal review:

1) Please share the SOC2 (latest) and the DPA draft PDF (links above look good but we need the actual PDFs for our registry).
2) Can you confirm the deletion audit log format (timestamped event with actor id + region + object id)? We will include the format spec in our internal ticketing.

If you can drop both PDFs and a short sample deletion audit record into the Drive link you sent, we’ll kick off our internal risk review this week. Pending that, we may ask for a short addendum limiting cross-region failover for our production workspace.

Thanks — Sara

(Forwarding to our procurement once the documents are uploaded.)
